and as for dogs, being man's best friend and all, have extremely humanoid facial expressions and will attempt to speak.

cats, to a lesser degree. cats have very expressive faces and limited ability to talk as humans.

weasels have their bouncy spines and 'ack aaack' and that's about it.

weasels are very aggressive and will chew on chewy, greasy mutts that lay around.

they also chew on human feet.

so i strongly sympathize with my dog when he is terrorized by weasels, who are clearly in the wrong. past dogs we've had were great with weasels off the bat - knowing to 'play lip' instead of 'play bite'. very gentle dogs. but our current dog had it in his head that he could play with a 2 pound animal as he could with a 70 pound dog. we had to go crazy training that out of him. i was really concerned for ages he'd hurt a weasel.

he never did.

but he gets chewed on and handles it as well as his dumb, greasy, grunting brain can. and i get chewed on, so i sympathize.

the weasels are the ones doing the biting. and i don't want to be unfair. time out doesn't seem to reach them. they just go flat and stare at me until time out has expired.

what do.
'you yell at the big animal out of principle'

I'm someone who's pretty good at placing themselves in other peoples' shoes. I would say I'm pretty good at imagining what others deal with.

But why the fuck would you want to be fat?????

I am absolutely perplexed as to why anyone, let alone the majority of people would let themselves become fat.

Sure, it's the easy thing to do. Eat whatever you want whenever you want, don't worry about how it's affecting your body, just kind of let yourself go because everyone else is.

But HOW can you live like that and be ok with it. People who have been fat from childhood, I can KIND of understand in the sense that they've always been fat and don't know anything different. But what honestly and truly baffles me are those who used to be thin/normal, let themselves get fat, and continue to let it just happen.

If I were fat for even a day, I would be absolutely miserable. I'd be sweaty, sluggish, feel stretched out and like there were weights strapped to me; any small form of physical exertion is a giant task. Looking lunpy and jiggly.... HOW can people be ok with this?

I can't help but remember when that shitlady Katie Hopkins purposely gained 42 lbs to see what it was like and prove that weight loss is absolutely possible. The whole time, she was absolutely miserable and ashamed of herself.

Imagine being disgusted by your own body. No, the answer is not to "learn to love it." Fucks sake, we as humans just are not built to be like that. If I were fat, all of my willpower would go to fixing it. There wouldn't be a donut in the world that could make me want to give up a healthy, fit body.

It has to be just more than complacency and utter apathy. I've had a few existential crises and felt pretty apathetic and nihilistic for a while, but even then, at no point, did I get FAT. The most weight I have possibly ever gained. from depression was ten pounds because I was eating my feelings and staying curled up in bed. This was before I really knew what CICO was and thought that whether you were fat or not depended on your genetics.

The most I have ever weighed was 120 lbs (at 5'3"). And it showed even though technically I wasn't overweight, but I felt absolutely disgusting and ashamed of myself nonetheless.

How can you willingly put yourself through being fat? Social stigma is the LEAST of your concerns; worse still is the joint pain, the struggle of breathing, dragging around so much extra weight, utter lack of flexibility, uncomfortable jiggling flesh, can't see your own fucking genitals, inability to fun physical movement, terrible sex.... Being ok with being fat: I just don't understand it.
